findings.title: build update sends a build past the newest release back to that older release when it is off its recipe
findings.cause: standing compares with `release < newest` alone, so a release past the newest reaches `unlike` and becomes OffRecipe, where its comment says a difference from the recipe matters at the newest release alone
findings.consequence: the project withdraws the tag of the current build and ai-ctl's recipe has since gained a patch or an option: build outdated says `off its recipe` and exits 4, and build update builds the older newest release with force and makes it current, which docs/commands.md:231 rules out for a build past the newest
findings.fix: compare by Ordering: Less is Behind, Greater is Current, and `unlike` counts at Equal alone
findings.test: a_build_past_the_newest_release_is_never_sent_back with `unlike` set expects Standing::Current, and gets OffRecipe on the code
findings.evidence: read: src/domain/build.rs:187-190, the comparison; src/domain/build.rs:552-562, its test covers at and behind, never past; src/application/build.rs:287, force from OffRecipe
findings.fingerprint: bugs | docs/commands.md + src/application/build.rs + src/domain/build.rs | Builder::update_project + standing + top level
findings.note: The verifier narrowed the consequence and replaced the fix: it holds on a clone made since the withdrawal, a clone that kept the tag rebuilding its own release. Ordering would say current of a build up refuses, so OffRecipe stays past the newest and update_project rebuilds the current build's own release.
findings.fixed_in: fix(build): rebuild a build off its recipe at its own release

findings.title: build outdated reads the tags under the configuration of the repository the user stands in
findings.cause: remote_tags runs git ls-remote with no -C, so in the command's working directory, and ls-remote loads the configuration of the repository around it; the adapter's other commands run in the clone, and git clone reads no such repository
findings.consequence: run from a repository whose .git/config rewrites the recipe's URL by url.<base>.insteadOf, the listing is that other repository's, on which build outdated gives its verdict and build update decides; run from one whose configuration git refuses, each project reads `cannot read its releases` and the command exits 1
findings.fix: run the listing in a directory that is no repository, git(Some(Path::new("/")), ...)
findings.test: build outdated run from a directory holding .git, with git a script that fails when its working directory holds one
findings.evidence: reproduced: git 2.56.0, from a repository with url.file:///<other>.insteadOf set to the llama.cpp URL, `git ls-remote --tags --refs -- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git 'b*'` printed the other repository's b999, and with -C / the real b12226; from a repository with a broken .git/config, exit 128 and `fatal: bad config line 6`, and with -C / exit 0
findings.note: Sibling path: git clone, the adapter's other command with no -C, was run from the same repository and is not steered by its configuration.
findings.fixed_in: fix(build): read the remote's tags outside the user's repository

findings.title: build update says no build is removed, where a build off its recipe is replaced in place
findings.cause: its help and docs/commands.md:260 say that no build is removed and that the build replaced stays for build use, while update_project passes force for OffRecipe and the store replaces the installed build of that id
findings.consequence: a user counting on build use to go back to a build off its recipe finds it replaced, the summary printing `built b12177` with no way back
findings.fix: say that a build off its recipe is replaced by its new build of the same release and that no other is removed, in the help and in docs/commands.md
findings.test: none: a text, and a_build_off_its_recipe_at_the_newest_release_is_built_again holds the behaviour
findings.evidence: read: src/presentation/cli.rs:103; docs/commands.md:260-261; src/application/build.rs:287 and 210; src/application/build.rs:3352, the test asserting the replacement
findings.fingerprint: the CLI's contract | docs/commands.md + src/application/build.rs + src/presentation/cli.rs | BuildAction + Builder::update_project + top level
findings.fixed_in: docs(build): say that build update replaces a build off its recipe

findings.title: a refusal reached through build update names --force, which build update does not take
findings.cause: the messages of taken name the option alone, written for build; update_project prints the same error in build update's summary, and BuildAction::Update has no --force
findings.consequence: for a project behind whose newest build is installed, the summary says `--force builds it again`; `ai-ctl build update --force`, on the command that printed it, stops at the command line with exit 2
findings.fix: name the whole command as Current::installed does, `ai-ctl build <project> --ref <id> --force`, in both messages of taken that reach build update
findings.test: a_project_behind_is_not_built_again_over_its_newest_build asserts the whole command in the failure
findings.evidence: read: src/application/build.rs:315 and 324, the bare option; src/application/build.rs:539-540, the whole command; src/presentation/cli.rs:102-110, no --force on Update; src/application/build.rs:3396-3399, the message expected
findings.note: Origin older by the blame of the message, right for build; it misleads only through build update, the phase's code, so the phase fixes it.
findings.fixed_in: fix(build): name the whole command in a refused build's remedy

findings.title: build update builds a release the project withdrew, where build outdated announced the newest the remote lists
findings.cause: fetch runs --prune --tags, which does not prune tags fetched through --tags, so a withdrawn tag stays in the clone; build takes its newest release from the clone, while build outdated takes it from the remote
findings.consequence: a project behind whose newest tag was withdrawn after the clone fetched it: build outdated says newest b12177, and build update builds and makes current the withdrawn b12200, which outdated then calls current
findings.fix: add --prune-tags to the fetch of GitSources::update, with finding 1's fix so that a build past the newest is not sent back when its tag goes
findings.test: after the upstream deletes a tag, a second fetch leaves it out of release_tags
findings.evidence: reproduced: git 2.56.0, a clone of a repository holding b1 and b2, `tag -d b2` upstream, then `git fetch --quiet --prune --tags --force origin` in the clone: `tag --list` still gives b1 and b2, `ls-remote --tags --refs origin` gives b1 alone; read: src/application/build.rs:142 and 331-332, the build's release from the clone's tags
findings.fingerprint: bugs | src/application/build.rs + src/infrastructure/git.rs | Builder::build + Builder::latest_release + GitSources::update + project_standing
findings.note: Registered at this review's close as older code and low; fixed in the closing pass of the roadmap, whose rule fixes what bears on its code, build update and build outdated among it: --prune-tags on the fetch of GitSources::update, with a test on a local upstream that withdraws a release and a tag that is not one.
findings.fixed_in: fix(build): drop the tags a project withdrew at each fetch
